predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: 'Sardinia was an imperial province of the Byzantine Empire until the 9th century'; the north-west of the island, twenty curatoriae, each ruled by a curator

successors.name: Republic of Genoa
successors.text: her territory was split among the Doria, Malaspina and Spinola families, who all held it from Genoa

successors.name: Judicate of Arborea
successors.text: the Judicate of Arborea gained some land

successors.name: Republic of Sassari
successors.text: Sassari became an autonomous city-state; it 'adopted a republican model of government in alliance with Genoa', which sent an annual podestà

ledger.x: 866: Logudoro appears in Cliopatria's first shape as the north-west of Sardinia; the page dates no founding.
1015: a Dénia army lands in the north of Sardinia.
1016: the Dénia camp is gone after 'one year'.
1259: Adelasia dies without an heir and Logudoro is broken up.

wars.name: Dénia invasion of Sardinia
wars.outcome: The Dénia army held a camp in the north of Sardinia for one year; the fleets of Pisa and Genoa reconquered the island; Mujahid's heir Ali Iqbal al-Dawla was captured and ransomed only in 1032.

wars.name: Genoese and Torres attack on Gallura
wars.outcome: In 1211 Comita III of Torres agreed to a treaty with Genoa to jointly conquer the island, Gallura first; Pisa struck back in 1212; Pope Honorius III forced a settlement on 1 December 1217.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on any page opened: the pages give twenty curatoriae and the neighbours' names only, and Cliopatria's outline follows modern provinces.
